newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. GOV. SIGNS POWER FOR JOBS LEGISLATION.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. GOV. SIGNS POWER FOR JOBS LEGISLATION.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki signed the Power of Jobs bill that passed the legislature last month, moving to stimulate new jobs by providing low-cost electricity to small businesses and not-for-profit corporations throughout the state, the Executive Office said.

The Power for Jobs Program will make available 400 megawatts of power, with half coming from New York State Power Authority's James A. Fitzpatrick Nuclear Power Plant on Lake Ontario and 200 megawatts purchased by the power authority through competitive bid.

The power will be allocated by the state's Economic Development Power Allocation Board, which must review and approve the applications filed by eligible businesses. Applications can be made within three years of the initiation of the program; each contract will be for three years.

The cost of the program will not be passed onto other electric ratepayers. It will be financed by a Gross Receipts Tax credit to private utilities and a contribution by the power authority, the Executive Office statement explained.

The new law provides a credit against the gross receipts tax for the net revenue lost by electric corporations as a result of furnishing low-cost power under the Power for Jobs program. In addition, the law authorizes the power authority to make a voluntary contribution to the state treasury to offset the program's cost.

Power rates for power from the power authority will be set at its economic development rate applicable to the service territory. As the competitive bidding program kicks in, the power authority rates will be melded together with the competitively bid rates for all customers.
The benefits of the program will be allocated throughout the state in proportion to the Gross Receipts Tax paid.
